verdict.line: You lose if you let Nasus freely stack Siphoning Strike and farm uncontested into a late-game deathball; you win by denying his CS and forcing fights before stacks 6.

brief.thesis: Nasus's entire power budget lives in permanent Q stacks that only grow when he lands Siphoning Strike (255 range, 8/7/6/5/4s cooldown) on a kill — deny those last hits and he simply doesn't scale. K'Sante's Q (Ntofo Strikes) hits in a line at 450 range and slows on every strike, which both outranges his farm tool and lets you contest CS directly. The measured data backs this: K'Sante holds the lane and solo-kill advantage here, so the matchup rewards pressuring him off CS early rather than passively farming alongside him.

theirWindow.when: After his W (Wither) lands on you
theirWindow.what: Wither decelerates your Movement and Attack Speed over time, so the longer you stay in range the worse it gets. Disengage immediately with E (Footwork)'s dash and shield rather than trying to trade through it.

yourWindow.when: While his W (Wither) is on cooldown
yourWindow.what: With no tool to slow or stick you, close in and poke with Q (Ntofo Strikes) for the line slow and stacks toward the 2-stack shockwave pull — your 450 range and 3.5s cooldown lets you answer his 255-range Q far more often than he can answer yours.

start.why: Highest win rate and pick rate start into Nasus — the extra sustain and magic resist buffer absorbs his Spirit Fire poke while you contest his CS.

boots.why: Higher measured win rate than Steelcaps here, and the tenacity directly cuts the duration of his W (Wither) slow, which is his only tool to stick you.

core.why: Gives you the waveclear and attack speed to contest his CS lane-wide while building toward Q stacks.
Stacking resistances scale through the long trades this matchup produces as both champions farm toward their stacks.
Highest win rate of the measured core paths (63.8%) and directly punishes Soul Eater lifesteal with grievous wounds.

he's stacked enough Siphoning Strikes to carry hard with attack speed late
you need more sustain in extended poke exchanges before committing

runes.keystoneWhy: Sustains you through the extended, attrition-style trades this lane produces while his Soul Eater passive does the same for him — you need the health scaling to not lose the war of attrition.

summoners.why: Ignite's highest-measured-win-rate pairing (55.6%) and its grievous wounds directly cuts into Soul Eater's lifesteal during the all-in windows your solo-kill advantage is built on.

playing.title: Contest every CS with Q
playing.detail: Nasus only gains stacks by landing Siphoning Strike (255 range) on a kill. Step up and poke the minion or Nasus himself with your 450-range Q to deny last hits and keep his stack count low.

playing.title: Track his Wither cooldown
playing.detail: W (Wither) is his only slow, on a 15/14/13/12/11s cooldown. While it's down he has no way to stick to you — that's your green light to all-in.

playing.title: Bank Q stacks for the pull
playing.detail: At 2 stacks of Ntofo Strikes your Q fires a shockwave that pulls him in. Save the second stack for when he's trying to walk away so you can re-engage for free.

playing.title: Charge W into his engage
playing.detail: Path Maker's charge-up phase reduces the damage you take before the dash lands its knockback and stun. Pre-charge it the moment he commits Wither so you tank the opener and still land your stun.

playing.title: All-in before level 6 stacks matter
playing.detail: Once R (All Out) is up at level 6, use its 250-range knockback to send him through terrain and dash in All Out for the bonus damage and healing — do this while his stack count is still small.

playing.title: Step out of Spirit Fire
playing.detail: His E zone reduces your Armor the longer you stand in it. Reposition with E (Footwork)'s dash and shield rather than fighting through the zone.

playing.title: Don't panic if he stacks late
playing.detail: The measured data shows this matchup is close to even overall — if you banked a lane or solo-kill lead early, your tank itemization is enough to hold even against a stacked Nasus.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, summoners, and all win rates above come from measured games on the current patch (16.19.1); the mechanical reasoning tying them to Nasus's Q-stack scaling and Wither timing is my own tactical read, not measured data.
